cards.text: A plague has just ended in Israel. Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He's got a job for them, friend, and it's the kind where you text the group chat, "Don't wait up."

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses and Eleazar to do?

cards.text: Big job. But the LORD isn't asking for every single person on this list.

cards.question: Who does the LORD want counted in this census?

answers.text: Men twenty and up who can serve in the army
Only the leaders of each family line
Every firstborn son from every tribe

cards.text: So Moses and Eleazar pass the order along: count the men, just like the LORD commanded. Hope somebody brought a pencil. A BIG one.

cards.question: Where is Israel when Moses and Eleazar give the order to count?

answers.text: The plains of Moab across from Jericho
Kadesh in the Desert of Zin
The shore of the Red Sea

cards.text: Then the count goes tribe by tribe, clan by clan, and it pauses for Dathan and Abiram, who rebelled with the followers of Korah, a man who led a rebellion against the LORD, and the earth swallowed them. Final total: 601,730 men. I used to count the dust falling in the junk drawer, and I never once made it past forty.
Count's done. Then the LORD tells Moses what all those names are for: the land is to be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, according to the number of names. See? The counting PAYS OFF.

cards.question: Under the LORD's plan, a large tribe gets a bigger inheritance than a small tribe.
The LORD says each tribe's inheritance of land must be divided by ___.

cards.text: The Levites get counted on their own: 23,000 males a month old or more. They aren't numbered with the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites. Their list even names Amram and Jochebed, the parents of Aaron, Moses and their sister Miriam.
Now, friend, there was an earlier count, taken by Moses and Aaron the priest in the Wilderness of Sinai. So how does this new list stack up against that old one?

cards.question: Most of the men counted at Sinai show up again in this new count on the plains of Moab.
The LORD had told the men of that first count that they would surely ___ in the wilderness.
Not one man from the Sinai count is left except two. Who are they?

cards.text: Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun, the only two left from that whole first count. Friend, that is a LONG time to keep answering roll call.

findings.problem: The summary card for the census stretch has 3 sentences, and the first one is a long run-on that packs in the tribe-by-tribe count, Dathan and Abiram, Korah's rebellion and the earth swallowing them. It should be trimmed to 1 to 2 sentences, with the Dathan and Abiram detail kept short.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The Levites card has 3 sentences and more than two beats: the Levite count, why they aren't counted with the other tribes, and Amram and Jochebed's family. It should be split into two cards or trimmed.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The last card repeats the answer card 15 just revealed (Caleb and Joshua, the only two left) and adds only their fathers' names. It doesn't move the passage forward. The fathers' names could go on an earlier card, or this card could end on a new beat.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
